image_prompt.text: Balanced team bases at opposite ends of the industrial arena, completely shielded from the opposing sniper tower's sightlines
Waist-high (3-4 studs) concrete barriers and full-body (7-8 studs) metal cover crates distributed evenly across every lane
Narrow transitions where the symmetrical lanes meet between the buildings, concentrating team fights onto contested middle ground
Metal catwalks, elevated platforms, and a sniper tower at each end, reachable only through exposed, predictable stairs and ladders
Several concrete-and-steel industrial structures entered from the street through doorways, with windows to fight out of

layout_placement.text: Mirrored team spawns at opposite ends of the map, placed out of the sniper towers' firing lines

notes: would have asked: sounds like a round-based team deathmatch map - mirrored bases at opposite ends, symmetrical lanes between them, crates and barriers for cover through every lane - plus the sniper towers and catwalks as elevated firing positions and the buildings as breachable structures you can go inside. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: the catwalks and elevated platforms are taken as supported tiered walkways rather than suspended over playable floor. Is anyone meant to fight underneath them? That makes it an overhanging build, which isn't ready yet.
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?
cover-elevated routed P0 + tiered rather than P2: its P2 is conditional on an actual overhang, and the prompt names catwalks and towers without saying play happens beneath them.

building-interior forces P3 because the buildings have doorways to pass through and windows to shoot from, so players go inside. P3 is not ready yet - if this has to ship now the buildings become facades with recessed doorways on P0 and the interiors are deferred.

"Tactical" here did not route to the Tactical Shooter preset. That preset is MilSim - a breach sequence of dead-end rooms with no mirrored bases - and this prompt asks for symmetrical lanes and bases at opposite ends, which is the arcade Team Deathmatch layout.
No option covers the request to expose tunable attributes for wall height, building count, and cover density; that is a generator parameter surface rather than anything placed in the map.
Modern industrial / urban warfare aesthetic in concrete and metal is a theme directive rather than a layout option, carried here so it reaches the image prompt.
building-interior used Shooter's own breachable-structure wording, which wins over the identical universal ID. No Universal Option was applied.
